resources.string: Notices when an application you set a daily limit for comes to the front, so BlockSocial Lite can tell you the limit is spent. It reads the name of that application and nothing else.

No daily limit yet. Set one and BlockSocial Lite will tell you when it is spent.
Time cannot be measured until usage access is granted.
The limit covers the whole day from midnight, including the time already spent today.

Android says this is on, yet the service is not answering. Some phones stop accessibility services in the background. Switch it off and on again in system settings, and if it keeps happening, allow BlockSocial Lite to run unrestricted in the battery settings of your phone.
The warning could not be drawn on top of the other application (%1$s). Your phone may be blocking it.
The one notification BlockSocial Lite shows is the quiet "limits are running" line. It is what stops the phone freezing the app in the background, and it is the only notification there is.
Everything below is read live from this phone. If a limit did not stop you, this page says why.
Nothing seen yet. Open a limited application and come back.

Lets BlockSocial Lite notice the moment a limited application comes to the front. It reads the name of that application and the moment it happened. Not the text on your screen, not your messages, not what you type.

Lets the phone keep BlockSocial Lite awake in the background. Without it, Android and especially Xiaomi firmware freeze the process after a while: the accessibility switch still says on, no screen changes reach the app, and limits silently stop stopping you. This is the single most common reason blocking does not work.
Lets BlockSocial Lite measure how long a limited application was in front today. Without it there is no daily limit, because there is nothing to count.
A quiet, permanent line that keeps the phone from freezing BlockSocial Lite while it watches for limited applications.
Keeping watch so your daily limits still stop you.
Your limit for today is spent
